title: Investigations on inter-splat boundaries of cold sprayed Ni–Cr coatings upon high temperature oxidation
InformationInFigures: Yes. Hardness and elastic modulus (Fig. 13), Some microstructure details (Fig. 11, 12, 7), Morphology (Fig. 6) Nozzle diagram (Fig. 3a)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: Mostly spherical with some satellite particles
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: grit blasted and ultrasonically cleaned using acetone. The grit blasting pressure was maintained as 3 bar. mirror polished

experimentalProperties.Particle_Critical_Velocity_Source: normalized for temperature dependency from a calculation using an equation provided by Assadi et al.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: coatings were cut using a slow saw cutting machine, and hot mounted for characterization. mirror polishing up to colloidal silica on hot mounted samples. etching was carried out on the samples. The chemical etchant contains 3:1 HCl and HNO3. The mounts were immersed in the etchant solution for 30 s. A berkovich nano indenter system at 5000 mN load was used to find the elastic moduli.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: presence of pull outs, a result of polishing, and evidence of poor inter-splat boundary state. undeformed powder observed, some refined splat boundaries.

Experiments.Notes: 873K/600C. Nozzle geometry is given in Fig. 3a but difficult to determine which side is exit and units not given.

experimentalProperties.Particle_Critical_Velocity_Source: normalized for temperature dependency from a calculation using an equation provided by Assadi et al.
experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Prior to cycling, coatings were heat treated at 800°C for an unspecified amount of time. In a thermal cyclic furnace, the sample was heated from room temperature up to 900°C in 20 mins, then held at 900°C for 60 mins, and cooled back to room temp in 20 mins. This cycle was repeated 150 times. after analysis every 50 cycles, another set of heat cycles were performed. the sample was heated from room temperature up to 1100°C in 20 mins, held at 1100°C for 40 mins, and the cooled to room temp in 10 mins. This cycle was repeated 735 times. Estimated time under high temperature is 1100h.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: coatings were cut using a slow saw cutting machine, and hot mounted for characterization. mirror polishing up to colloidal silica on hot mounted samples. etching was carried out on the samples. The chemical etchant contains 3:1 HCl and HNO3. The mounts were immersed in the etchant solution for 30 s. A berkovich nano indenter system at 5000 mN load was used to find the elastic moduli.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: very little weight change from the first 150 cycles. after roughly 650 thermal cycles, oxidation occured leading to weight gain. However, after 650 cycles weight loss due to spallation occured. exhibit different oxide scales with different morphology. Most of the oxide grains are in pyramidal in shape and not continuous. oxide scales delaminated from the coatings up to 885 cycles. the oxide layers that detatched had a top layer with a columnar structure and the bottom layer with a granular structure. formation of NiO, Cr2O3, and NiCr2O4 (Spinel) were identified and confirmed, and the amount of NiO and Cr2O3 decreased as a function of process gas temp. the spinel amount in the coating increased with the higher process gas temp.

Experiments.Notes: 873K/600C TC. Values reported are after 150 cycles of 900C Nozzle geometry is given in Fig. 3a but difficult to determine which side is exit and units not given.
